claims.claim: Independent U.S. government records confirm Texas Instruments received a final CHIPS award of up to $1.61 billion supporting more than $18 billion of investment through the end of the decade across three new U.S. 300mm fabs in Texas and Utah.

NIST describes the supported fabs as high-volume 300mm capacity for analog and embedded-processing semiconductors, with Sherman targeting 65nm-130nm production and Lehi targeting 28nm-65nm production, materially corroborating the domestic-capacity and supply-resilience thesis independently of issuer-origin evidence.

risks.risk: CHIPS direct funding is milestone-dependent and does not itself prove fab utilization, customer demand, or attractive incremental returns on invested capital.

unknowns.unknown: Current utilization, realized milestone disbursements, and incremental returns on the new 300mm capacity still require Alpha underwriting.
